title.en: Up in the air so blue

text.en: Robert Louis Stevenson's poem The Swing describes the joy of going up and down on a swing, seeing rivers, trees, cattle and the countryside from high above. In this chapter you will read the poem, learn the words pleasantest, cattle and countryside, build longer sentences step by step, learn words that can be both a noun and a verb, practise the w sound and use position words.

The poet asks how you like to go up in a swing, up in the air so blue, and answers that it is the pleasantest thing a child can do. The poet says the swing goes up and over the wall, high enough to see far across the countryside. From up there the child can see rivers, trees, cattle and all, which means farm animals like cows and buffaloes. Then the swing comes down and the child looks at the green garden and the brown roof. The child goes flying up again, and the poem ends with the swing going up in the air and down.
The poet clearly enjoys swings. The lines saying it is the pleasantest thing a child can do tell us so. The air is called blue because the sky is blue, and the child is swinging high up toward it. The poem has a rhythm that moves up and down, just like a swing. Rhyming words in the poem are swing and thing, and wall and all. Words that rhyme with swing are ring, king, sing and spring.
Pleasantest means the most enjoyable. Cattle are farm animals like cows and bulls. Countryside is the land outside towns and cities with fields, villages and farms.
We can make a sentence longer by adding details one by one. Jeevan waited. Jeevan waited for the bus. Jeevan waited for the bus all morning. Jeevan waited for the bus all morning in the rain. Finally: Jeevan waited for the bus all morning in the rain because his scooter was in the garage being repaired. Each new part answers a question: for what, how long, where and why.
Some words can be a verb in one sentence and a noun in another. I swing on a swing. The first swing is a verb, meaning to move forward and back, and the second is a noun, an object. The dance begins in an hour (noun). My friends and I dance when we are happy (verb). I like to play kho-kho (verb). We will watch a play tomorrow (noun). Can you answer the questions (verb)? I know the answer (noun). There is a fly on the wall (noun). My friends fly kites (verb). The waves did not let us finish our sandcastle (noun). She waves to her siblings (verb).
A tongue twister is a sentence that is hard to say fast. How much wood would a woodchuck chuck if a woodchuck could chuck wood? To say the w sound, make an O shape with your lips. For v, touch your upper teeth to your lower lip. Practise: wet, wait, win, wise and white with the O shape, and vet, vine, valley, fever and fewer with the teeth on the lip.
Prepositions are words used before a noun or pronoun to show place, time or direction. On, beside, between, above, in front of, behind and under are position words. A ladybug between two flower pots, a butterfly above a flower, a honeybee on a flower, an ant on a leaf and a caterpillar on a flowerpot are examples. You can write a few sentences about what you enjoy in your free time, such as drawing, reading or playing kho-kho. Draw a magical swing that can take you anywhere, like outer space or a jungle, and write about the adventure.

problem.en: Make the sentence longer: The boy ran. Add where and why.

text.en: Add where: The boy ran to the park.
Add why: The boy ran to the park because he wanted to play.
So the longer sentence is: The boy ran to the park because he wanted to play.

why.en: Each added part gives more detail.

problem.en: Is play a noun or a verb: We will watch a play tomorrow.

text.en: Look at the word before play.
A play is a story acted on a stage.
So play is a noun here.

why.en: In I like to play it is a verb.

prompt.en: Say what the poem is about and how you can tell the poet loves swings.

requiredIdeas.en: Going up and down on a swing
Seeing rivers, trees, cattle and the countryside
The pleasantest thing a child can do

commonMisconceptions.en: The poet is afraid of swings
The poem is about a boat

points.en: The poem describes the joy of swinging high above the countryside.
Pleasantest means most enjoyable; cattle are farm animals.
A sentence can be made longer by adding details.
Some words, like play, dance and fly, can be nouns or verbs.
Position words like above, between and under show where things are.
